evidence_against: The API sequence is mixed rather than uniformly bearish: over 72 hours BTC returned +0.36% while ETH returned -0.03%; over 24 hours BTC returned +0.63% and ETH -0.34%. BTC net aggressive quote flow was positive over the reported 12h, 24h, and 72h windows, although ETH flow was negative over 24h.

Direct ETH/BTC hourly closes were above 0.0300 in 161 of 168 observations, with only six below; the latest close was 0.03015 and five consecutive closes were on the same side. This supports persistence above the level, though not ETH-relative strength.

The prior capture’s breadth proxy showed 42 advancers versus 23 previously. This is not directly comparable to the later rich-breadth observation: membership hashes and observation times differ, and the rich-breadth observation was after the stated API cutoff.

BTC and ETH open interest declined over the reported 12h, 24h, and 72h windows. That is consistent with deleveraging as well as weakening participation, and does not by itself establish forced distribution.

Action Compass calibration is descriptive and low-confidence: warning cohorts are small in some periods, overlapping freezes are not independent, and nonwarning downside outcomes also include adverse moves. It provides no validated trigger or present warning classification.
evidence_for: The latest API 12h window (actual span 9h) showed BTC -0.58%, ETH -0.64%, and ETH/BTC -0.03%; the 24h window (actual span 21h) showed ETH/BTC -0.92%. ETH underperformed BTC across these windows.

In the latest capture versus its predecessor, BTC and ETH mark prices fell about 0.28% and 0.27%. BTC spot depth imbalance changed from +0.30 to -0.05 and taker quote imbalance from +0.46 to -0.77; ETH taker imbalance fell from +0.51 to +0.04. These are brief venue-specific observations, not durable flow measures.

The latest capture’s 100-asset breadth proxy had 42 advancers and 57 decliners. A separate later rich-breadth snapshot reported 38 advancers, 61 decliners, and a -0.38% median 24h return, but it is after the decision cutoff and remains proxy-only evidence.
Sentiment scores fell between captures: BTC 52 to 40.5, ETH 47 to 38.5, and market 47 to 41.5. Latest classifications were BTC Neutral, ETH Fear, and market Neutral.

Rotation context is weak and method-dependent: BlockchainCenter scores were 49, 47, and 37 at 30d, 90d, and 365d, all between published thresholds; the separate CMC 90d score was 58, with an 11-point method dispersion. Neither establishes broad rotation.
The latest settled ETF row available was dated October 9: BTC +21.1 and ETH -56.1 in reported units. It is roughly 79 hours old at the stated cutoff and cannot establish current flows.

Current options-chain moneyness-bucket put IV exceeded call IV for the near expiries shown. The capture is current-chain-only, has no equivalent historical snapshot, and explicitly is not 25-delta skew; it is limited downside-hedging context, not confirmation.

Leverage stress is not established by the observed falling open interest and modest positive funding; the hypotheses remain unproven.

This is more consistent with a pause and uneven participation than a confirmed distribution or structural breakdown. A later rich-breadth snapshot is after the stated cutoff and is not used as cutoff-time confirmation. No typed warning is established by these shadow observations.
uncertainties: The nominal 1h API horizon is unavailable because no anchor met tolerance; the 4h horizon has only a 1h actual span and two samples. The immediate sequence is therefore limited.

The stated decision cutoff is 2026-10-13T19:14:44Z. The rich-breadth snapshot and passive pullback-forensics capture occurred after that cutoff; the former is excluded from cutoff-time evidence, and neither is used to establish state.
The latest settled ETF row is from October 9 and is about 79 hours old at cutoff. Missing intervening sessions are not inferred.
Breadth observations are point-in-time proxy universes with differing membership hashes; canonical broad-alt and large-cap breadth remain unconfirmed.
Liquidation aggregates are lower bounds from a fragile legacy REST source with unverified completeness. Current options data have no equivalent historical snapshot.
The supplied evidence does not provide a canonical cycle phase or warning, and the calibration’s small, overlapping samples cannot be treated as independent events or as threshold validation.
